neighbours.label: a mid-sentence 'when' (or 'except') opening a habitual or conditional circumstance clause ('when not in use', 'even when you are asleep'), as against interrogative or embedded-question 'when'
fire: Always unplug the kettle when not in use to save electricity.
Our cat hides under the bed whenever there are visitors, and when it thunders.
Keep the lid of the paint tin sealed when you are not using it.
The heart keeps beating steadily even when we are fast asleep.
Store the bicycle indoors when it is not being ridden.
My phone gets hot when it is charging overnight.
Fold the chairs away when not needed so the hall stays tidy.
Dogs can feel anxious when their owners leave the house.
quiet: Can you tell me when the kettle was bought?
Nobody knows exactly when our cat first arrived at the house.
When did you last open the paint tin in the garage?
Doctors still ask when the heart first starts to beat in the womb.
I forgot when the bicycle was last ridden.
Do you remember when you got this phone?
The caretaker asked when the chairs would be delivered.
When will the owners come back to collect their dog?

predictions: fire 0.4-0.8 on 'when' or the 'not' after it; question 'when' and 'wonder when' 0.0-0.05
